key: A weather forecaster on the evening news
name: ch11_forecast_vs_sure_uncle
alt: Split picture: a TV weatherman calmly shows a 70 percent rain chance, while an uncle at a family lunch table insists it will not rain as heavy rain pours outside the window.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a television set on a low wooden stand shows an evening weather report; inside the screen a friendly forecaster in his 40s (light blue shirt, neat moustache) stands beside a simple map of the Tamil Nadu coast with a grey rain cloud icon, gesturing openly with one palm, relaxed and modest. Above the TV, a bold label reads "70%". Below the TV, small sun-and-cloud icons suggest either outcome is fine. RIGHT panel: a family lunch at a dining table with steel plates, rice and sambar; a portly uncle in his 50s (white kurta, spectacles, thick moustache) half-rises from his chair, one finger jabbing the air, mouth wide mid-shout, absolutely certain. Behind him a window shows heavy diagonal rain lines and a dark cloud, and the rest of the family (an aunt in a green sari, a teenage nephew) glance from the window to him with raised eyebrows. A red exclamation badge floats near the window. Above the right panel a bold label reads "100% SURE". A small speech bubble from the uncle shows a crossed-out cloud. Warm indoor light on the right against grey stormy light outside; gently comic mood: the modest forecaster keeps face, the certain uncle has just lost it.

key: A good cricket coach at a Mumbai maidan
name: ch11_coach_grip_lower
alt: A cricket coach on a city maidan gently shows a teenage batter where to hold the bat lower, and the boy, after a few balls, smiles as if it was his own discovery.
scene: A wide daytime view of a dusty open maidan in Mumbai, with distant old stone buildings and a few other net sessions in the background. In the CENTRE-LEFT, a teenage batter (about 15, white cricket clothes, pads, a blue cap) stands at a practice crease holding his bat. Beside him, an experienced coach in his 50s (tracksuit, whistle on a cord, grey hair, calm half-smile) does not point or scold; he holds an open palm low beside the bat handle, suggesting. A circular inset bubble at upper left zooms in on the bat handle: two hands on the grip, a dashed outline of the old high position and a curved arrow showing the hands sliding down to the lower position. Above the inset a bold label reads "TRY THIS". On the RIGHT, a young bowler runs in with a red ball, and a small row of ten ball icons with green ticks runs along the bottom, showing the balls played. Above the batter's head a light bulb and a speech bubble with a big smile show his own realisation; the coach stands back with arms folded, quietly pleased. Morning sunlight, friendly mood: the coach proves his point without ever announcing it.

key: A customer storms into a mobile repair
name: ch11_repair_shop_we_erred
alt: In a small mobile repair shop, an angry customer holds up an overheating phone and the owner opens his palms and offers that they may have missed something, and the customer calms down.
scene: A street-front view of a narrow mobile phone repair shop in a busy Delhi market: a glass counter full of phone covers and chargers, a wall of small drawers, a magnifying lamp and a tiny screwdriver set on the counter. On the LEFT, a customer in his 30s (office shirt, sleeves rolled, bag strap across chest) leans forward over the counter holding up a phone with wavy heat lines and a small red thermometer badge rising from it; his eyebrows are angled, but a dashed arrow from his head to a softer face beside it shows the anger draining away. On the RIGHT, behind the counter, the shop owner in his 40s (grey checked shirt, spectacles pushed up on his forehead) holds both palms open at chest height, head slightly bowed, attentive, a notepad ready. A speech bubble from the owner reads in a bold label "MAYBE WE MISSED IT". In the top left corner, a small inset shows the same customer later, smiling on his phone with his cousin beside him and a green tick. No shop signs or brand names. Warm afternoon market light, mood shifting from tense to calm.

key: A junior doctor on her first ward round
name: ch11_ward_round_wrong_dose
alt: Split picture of a hospital ward round: on the left a junior doctor bluntly corrects a red-faced consultant in front of students; on the right she suggests checking the formulary and he nods.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a big government hospital ward with iron beds, pale green walls and a ceiling fan, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a senior consultant in his 50s (white coat, grey hair, stethoscope, file in hand) stands red-faced and stiff, with a small red exclamation badge above him; facing him, a young junior doctor in her 20s (white coat over a blue salwar kameez, hair in a bun) points flatly at the chart. Behind them, a cluster of students in white coats look away awkwardly. Above this panel a bold label reads "BLUNT". RIGHT panel: the same two people at the same bedside, but she holds a thick reference book open towards him with a modest, tilted head, and he leans in to read, nodding, his face calm; a small green tick floats above the open book and a dosage chart shows a downward arrow towards a lower number. Above this panel a bold label reads "GENTLE". A patient rests quietly in the bed between them in both halves. Bright daytime ward light; mood: the same fact, two very different rooms.

key: Tell someone in Kolkata that Hyderabadi
name: ch11_biryani_potato_debate
alt: Two friends with plates of biryani; when one says the other's city biryani is worse because of the potato, the other suddenly defends it with a bubble full of reasons and a city badge.
scene: A medium shot at a small restaurant table with a checked tablecloth and two steel plates of biryani. On the LEFT, a young man in his 20s (yellow T-shirt, casual, smug grin) points with a spoon at the plate opposite, his own plate showing plain biryani rice and a chicken piece. On the RIGHT, a woman in her late 20s (red-bordered white sari blouse and a cotton kurta, bindi) sits bolt upright, one hand protectively curved around her plate, which has a large golden potato sitting proudly on top of the rice; her expression is indignant, eyebrows high. Above her head rises a large thought bubble crowded with tiny items: a family photo of a grandmother at a stove, a list with numbered lines, a heart, and the potato again. Beside the bubble a bold label reads "MY BIRYANI". A small badge pinned to her kurta shows a heart. A dashed arrow from his pointing spoon to the potato has a small spark where it lands, showing the remark lighting the reflex. In the background, other diners look over with amused faces. Warm evening restaurant light, playful mood: it was never about the potato.

key: Your cousin proudly shows the family the
name: ch11_cousin_car_overpaid
alt: Split picture: an aunt tells a cousin he overpaid for his used car and he argues back; later a friend admires the car and the cousin sighs that he probably overpaid.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man (late 20s, sky-blue shirt, car keys in hand) and the same small silver second-hand hatchback in both halves, parked outside a Pune apartment building. LEFT panel: an aunt in her 50s (maroon sari, spectacles, hand on hip) points sharply at the car's price sticker, mouth open mid-lecture; the cousin stands with arms crossed tight, chin raised, defending, a speech bubble from him showing a speedometer with a low mileage needle. A red cross badge floats between them. Above this panel a bold label reads "ATTACKED". RIGHT panel: a week later, a friend of the same age (green T-shirt) leans on the car admiringly with a warm smile and a heart near his head; the cousin now stands relaxed, rubbing the back of his neck, looking down with a sheepish smile, a small speech bubble from him showing a price tag with an upward arrow and a sigh mark. Above this panel a bold label reads "ADMITS". Late-afternoon light on both sides; mood: pressure makes him defend, warmth lets him admit.

key: A school debate champion from Chandigarh
name: ch11_debate_champ_canteen
alt: Split picture of a college canteen: first a debate champion lectures at an emptying table, then the same student listens with a softer face and classmates gather round him for advice.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a busy college canteen with long tables, steel tea glasses and plates of samosa, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a confident student about 19 (navy hoodie, neat hair) stands at the table jabbing a finger, mouth wide, a speech bubble filled with a trophy icon; around him the chairs are empty, and two classmates walk away towards the edge of the panel carrying their tea, one rolling her eyes. A small hourglass near the table suggests how tiring it is. Above this panel a bold label reads "ALWAYS WINS". RIGHT panel: the same student, now seated, leaning slightly forward with an open palm and a gentle, listening expression; three classmates (a girl in a yellow kurta, a boy in a striped T-shirt, a girl with spectacles) sit close around him, one speaking while he nods, a small green tick and a heart floating above the group. His small speech bubble reads in bold "I MIGHT BE WRONG" placed above the panel as its label. Warm canteen lighting with ceiling fans; mood: from winning arguments to winning people.

key: A newly married daughter-in-law in a joi
name: ch11_kitchen_amma_layout
alt: A young daughter-in-law asks her mother-in-law over tea what slows her down in the kitchen; later the proud mother-in-law shows a guest the new spice shelf beside the stove.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same busy joint-family kitchen in Lucknow, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: early morning, the young daughter-in-law in her mid-20s (pink salwar kameez, dupatta, small mangalsutra) and her mother-in-law in her 60s (cream sari with a maroon border, grey bun, spectacles) sit on low stools sharing glasses of chai. The daughter-in-law leans in, listening, with a question mark badge above her; a thought bubble from Amma shows her walking far across the kitchen to a high shelf of masala tins. Above this panel a bold label reads "ASK". A small dashed arrow in the bubble suggests the tins moving next to the stove. RIGHT panel: a week later, Amma stands proudly beside the gas stove with a new low spice rack of round masala tins right next to the burners, one arm sweeping towards it as she shows a visiting neighbour, who claps; the daughter-in-law stands quietly at the back with a small, content smile. Above this panel a bold label reads "AMMA'S IDEA". Warm morning kitchen light, steel vessels gleaming; mood: the plan is used because it became hers.

key: A textile exporter in Tiruppur gets a ca
name: ch11_tiruppur_inspection
alt: In a warehouse an exporter watches a quality inspector check cotton shirts against a silk-garment standard, and asks him to show what he looks for until he realises the mismatch.
scene: A wide interior view of a buyer's warehouse with tall metal shelving, cardboard cartons and a long inspection table under hanging lights. On the table lies a stack of folded cotton shirts, a few with small red cross tags. In the CENTRE, a quality inspector in his 40s (grey work jacket, ID tag on a lanyard, spectacles) holds a magnifying glass over a shirt seam, frowning in concentration. Beside him, a clipboard on the table shows a checklist with a small silk scarf icon at the top. On the LEFT, a businesswoman exporter in her 40s (teal cotton sari, reading glasses, small handbag) stands beside him, leaning in with genuine interest, one hand gesturing gently at the shirt as she asks to be shown. A dashed arrow runs from the silk icon on the clipboard to the cotton shirts, with a large question mark badge at its midpoint, showing the wrong standard being applied. Above, a bold label reads "WRONG STANDARD". Small labels on the two items read "SILK" by the clipboard icon and "COTTON" by the shirt stack. On the RIGHT, a green tick hovers over a sealed carton ready to ship. Cool warehouse light; mood: patient curiosity lets him find the mistake himself.

key: A selector for a Ranji Trophy team is as
name: ch11_selector_fair_judge
alt: At a press table a cricket selector praises a fast bowler's record while a journalist waves a newspaper of the bowler's criticism, the two matters kept in separate boxes.
scene: A press-conference scene in a cricket stadium media room with a long table, two microphones on stands and a plain backdrop. In the CENTRE, a cricket selector in his 50s (navy blazer over a white shirt, grey hair, calm expression) sits behind the table, gesturing with an open hand towards a large board on the LEFT that shows a fast bowler in white kit mid-delivery, with a speed arrow and three green ticks beneath. Above that board a bold label reads "BOWLING". On the RIGHT, a journalist in her 30s (yellow kurta, press ID card, notepad) stands holding up a newspaper whose page shows only a small angry face icon and a big exclamation mark. Between the selector and the newspaper stands a thin vertical divider wall, and above the newspaper a bold label reads "OPINION". The selector's shoulders are relaxed, a small shrug drawn with two curved lines, as he keeps the two matters apart. A dashed arrow from the newspaper bends away and stops at the divider with a small grey stop bar, showing that the criticism does not leak into the selection. Bright media-room light; calm, fair mood.
